title: KV ghost objects causing GPU resident-accounting surge and inference OOMs — runtime patch + canary rollout
creator: Sofia Chen
description: Multiple customers across Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployments reported sudden GPU OOMs during long-tail inference sessions. Root cause analysis shows a combination of KV cache "ghost objects" (unaccounted references in the session slab allocator) and slab fragmentation that allows resident GPU memory accounting to underreport freeable pages. The end result: periodic memory accounting spikes that tip nodes into OOM and trigger session evictions. This ticket tracks the customer escalations, the short-term mitigations we applied, and the runtime patch and rollout plan to permanently fix the refcounting + reclamation paths.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Run multi-session inference workload with large KV cache churn (long context, many short-lived prefixes)
2) Enable session-level KV caching and set kv_eviction_threshold to default (0.6)
3) Observe steady increase in gpu_resident_bytes reported by runtime metrics, with periodic jumps that do not correspond to live tensor allocations
4) Trigger high-concurrency requests (>=120 concurrent streams) until node OOMs or scheduler evicts sessions
observed_behavior: OOMs occur without proportional CPU-side allocation increases
kvcache object count diverges from live session handles (ghost objects in slab lists)
fragmentation metrics show many small free slabs that cannot be coalesced due to stale tombstones
mitigation_actions: 1) Emergency config push to increase kv_eviction_aggressiveness to 0.35 for affected clusters
2) Rolling restart of 3x dedicated clusters to force session reclamation (hosted: gradual restart with traffic drain)
3) Temporarily disabled long-lived prefix caching for two high-traffic customers (with customer notification)
4) Added short-term alert: kv_handle_count / session_count > 1.4 triggers p0 pager
proposed_fix: Implement deterministic KV handle refcount reconciliation and tombstone sweep during slab compaction. The patch adds a fast-path decrement when sessions close and a background coalescer that merges adjacent free slabs when freeable_slabs > threshold. Also add assertion and metric (kvcache_reconciled_count) to detect future divergence.
canary_plan: Canary will run on two low-risk hosted clusters (us-west-2 small) for 48 hours with synthetic KV churn and production sampling for impacted customers. If no regression and kvcache_reconciled_count > 0 on canary, proceed to staggered rollout: hosted -> dedicated low-burst -> dedicated high-burst -> private with customer opt-in. Rollout window per cohort: 24 hours with rollback on >2% increase in 5m OOM rate.
